ruled_out_vectors.vector: C1: FullMath.mulDiv phantom overflow — intermediate 512-bit multiplication produces incorrect results
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: mulDiv correctly handles phantom overflow via 512-bit intermediate computation. Forge fuzz (25 runs uint128 inputs) and symbolic check_ functions verify: result * denominator <= numerator * multiplier + denominator - 1. All pass.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C2: mulDivRoundingUp produces incorrect result less than mulDiv
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge fuzz (25 runs): mulDivRoundingUp >= mulDiv for all inputs, difference <= 1. Halmos check_ confirms symbolically.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C3: FixedHelper._splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight — 1-wei swap produces free tokens or bypasses dust validation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 1-wei input with fee rounds to 0 after fee, pool correctly reverts with FixedPool__ZeroValueSwap. Large inputs capped by reserves. Dust validation at lines 1670-1673 and 1698-1702 catches split rounding errors. 84 integration tests pass.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C4: FixedHelper._calculateSwapByInputFixed — max fee or zero liquidity height bypass
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 99.99% fee (9999 BPS) correctly leaves near-zero for swap. Pool rejects zero-value swaps. Integration test with max fee passes.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C5: FixedHelper._calculateSwapByOutputFixed — output exceeds full reserve
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Output capped by expectedReserve at line 1020-1021. Full-reserve output swap test passes. Round-trip fuzz confirms no profitable arbitrage.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C6: Fixed pool add/remove liquidity round-trip creates tokens from rounding
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Add 50K then remove all — user balance <= original + 2 wei (rounding dust to protocol). Integration test confirms protocol keeps rounding dust.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C7: DynamicHelper.computeSwap — tick boundary overshoot causing price to jump past tick into incorrect range
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge tests verify: (1) single-tick range swap stays within bounds, (2) exact boundary swap with 0.3% fee does not overshoot target price. Price is bounded by step.sqrtPriceNextX96 in SwapMath.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C8: DynamicHelper._getTokensOwed — uint128 truncation on large feeGrowth * liquidity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: With liquidity=1 and max feeGrowth, result = max256/Q128 = max128 (fits). With max liquidity and delta=1, result = 0 (below truncation threshold). Halmos check_ confirms: for all uint128 inputs, mulDiv(delta, liq, Q128) <= type(uint128).max. Theoretical overflow requires astronomically unrealistic fee accumulation.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C9: DynamicHelper._updatePosition — 0 liquidity change allows extracting more fees than owed
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee calculation with Q128 feeGrowth per unit liquidity correctly returns expected tokens. Fuzz (25 runs) confirms no uint128 overflow in fee cast.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C10: DynamicHelper._crossTick — fee growth outside flip incorrect, causing wrong fee distribution on direction change
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Cross tick correctly computes: newOutside = global - outside. Verified forward/reverse flip consistency. Unchecked wrapping behavior is by design (Uniswap V3 pattern). LiquidityNet applied correctly in both directions (+/-).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C11: SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPrice — zero amount, zero price, zero liquidity edge cases allow extraction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Zero amount returns same price. Zero price and zero liquidity correctly revert. Price direction verified: zeroForOne decreases, oneForZero increases. Halmos check_ confirms direction property symbolically.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C12: getAmount0Delta/getAmount1Delta — wrong rounding direction allows user to extract dust
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Equal prices return 0. RoundUp >= RoundDown for all tested liquidity levels. Max liquidity does not revert. Halmos check_ confirms rounding direction symbolically for uint64 liquidity range.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C13: SwapMath.computeSwapStep — free tokens when amountRemaining=1 or extreme fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: amountIn + feeAmount >= amountOut for all tested inputs (1 wei, max, 0% fee, 99.99% fee). Output swap also safe. Halmos check_ confirms: no free tokens for uint64 amounts.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C14: TickMath round-trip — getSqrtPriceAtTick -> getTickAtSqrtPrice loses precision
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Round-trip exact at every 1000th tick from MIN_TICK to MAX_TICK (1775 ticks). MIN_TICK -> MIN_SQRT_RATIO, MAX_TICK -> MAX_SQRT_RATIO. Invalid ticks revert. Halmos check_ confirms round-trip for all int24.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C15: BitMath.MSB/LSB — incorrect result for edge values causes wrong tick bitmap navigation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: MSB(2^n) == n for all n in [0,254]. MSB(max) == 255. MSB(1) == 0. MSB(0) and LSB(0) revert. Halmos check_ confirms MSB/LSB of all powers of 2.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C16: LiquidityMath.addDelta — underflow or overflow allows creating/destroying liquidity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Positive addition works. Negative subtraction works. Underflow (50, -51) reverts. Overflow (max, +1) reverts. int128.min reverts. Halmos check_ confirms safe subtraction path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C17: FeeHelper — 100% fee creates free tokens or fee exceeds input
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100% fee (10000 BPS) on input: amountIn=0, amountOut=0, feeAmount=full input. Entire input becomes fee, no output generated. This is by design. Fee can never exceed input (mulDivRoundingUp bounded by input).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C18: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput — rounding up causes maker to overpay taker
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB uses mulDivRoundingUp (rounds UP for output), while SingleProvider uses mulDiv (rounds DOWN). CLOB output >= SP output always (fuzz 25 runs). Difference is at most 2 wei per trade. Not exploitable: maker sets own price; taker benefits from rounding. Economic impact ~4500 wei across 100 fills at favorable prices.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C19: SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 — overflow on extreme inputs produces near-zero price
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Both zeros return 2^96. amount1=0 returns MIN_SQRT_RATIO. amount0=0 returns MAX_SQRT_RATIO. Equal amounts return ~2^96 (within 0.1%). Large inputs handled without revert. Overflow to 0 caught by MIN_SQRT_RATIO/MAX_SQRT_RATIO bounds in pool types.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C20: SingleProviderHelper — round-trip calculateFixedInput/Output produces profit
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: calculateFixedInput rounds DOWN (mulDiv), calculateFixedOutput rounds UP (mulDivRoundingUp). Fuzz confirms: forward(amountIn) -> reverse(amountOut) always returns <= amountIn. Both directions tested. Edge cases: price=1 produces 0 output (safe), price=MAX handled.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C21: Medusa fuzzing on FixedPoolType — property violations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Medusa failed to initialize: constructor arguments for FixedPoolType not provided. Contract requires deployment context. Logged as tool error.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: not-applicable: Medusa requires constructor args for FixedPoolType deployment

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C22: Medusa fuzzing on DynamicPoolType — property violations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Medusa ran 333,893 calls (50K test limit), 37 corpus items, 353 branches explored. 14/14 assertion tests passed, 0 failures found. All state-changing functions covered.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: not-applicable: Medusa run via CLI, no violations found

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C23: INV-SW02 No Profitable Round-Trip — swap A->B then B->A yields more than started
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Dynamic pool: fuzz (25 runs) confirms amountOut0 <= original amountIn for all token0->token1->token0 paths. Fixed pool: integration fuzz (bound 1000-50Ke6) confirms USDC balance never increases after round-trip.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C24: INV-SW03 Rounding Favors Protocol — 1-wei swaps drain pool
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Dynamic: 100 sequential 1-wei swaps accumulate 0 total output (fee rounds to total input). Fixed: 1-wei swaps correctly revert with ZeroValueSwap. 1000-wei swaps (50 iterations) do not drain pool. Protocol always receives more than it gives.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C25: INV-E01 Fee Monotonicity — feeGrowthGlobal decreases across swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100 sequential swaps (alternating directions, increasing amounts) with 0.3% fee: cumulative fee is strictly monotonically non-decreasing. Each swap adds positive feeAmount to cumulative total.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C26: Cetus-pattern precision extraction — crafted tick_index causes overflow in sqrt price, producing near-zero price enabling massive withdrawal
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: MIN_TICK produces MIN_SQRT_RATIO (4295128739, non-zero). MAX_TICK produces MAX_SQRT_RATIO. 100 ticks near MIN_TICK all produce non-zero prices. computeRatioX96 with extreme inputs returns 0 (overflow protection), but 0 is caught by MIN_SQRT_RATIO bounds check in pool types (line 328-330 of SingleProviderPoolType).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C27: Balancer-pattern rounding direction — wrong-direction rounding allows dust-loop drain via repeated add/remove
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: For all liquidity levels 1-100: addAmount >= |removeAmount| for both tokens. Protocol keeps rounding dust. SqrtPriceMath uses roundUp for add (user pays more) and roundDown for remove (user receives less). No single wrong-direction rounding found.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C28: ERC-4626 first depositor inflation — 1-wei LP deposit + donation allows stealing from second LP
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: With liquidity=1: addAmount >= removeAmount for both tokens. Rounding favors protocol even at minimum liquidity. DynamicPoolType does not use share-based accounting (uses direct liquidity amounts), so ERC-4626 inflation pattern does not apply.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C29: Hook price manipulation — malicious hook returns extreme price (0, max, 1 wei) to SingleProviderPoolType
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SingleProviderPoolType.swapByInput (line 328-330) explicitly bounds-checks: if (sqrtPriceCurrentX96 < MIN_SQRT_RATIO || sqrtPriceCurrentX96 >= MAX_SQRT_RATIO) revert. Hook returning 0 or type(uint160).max is rejected. Guard holds.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: Tick crossing at exact boundary — liquidity not properly added/removed
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: LiquidityMath.addDelta correctly handles both positive (crossing right) and negative (crossing left) liquidityNet. Test confirms: 1e18 + 5e17 = 1.5e18 and 1e18 - 5e17 = 0.5e18. Underflow protection via revert.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H3: 100% fee asymmetry — input accepts 100% fee but output rejects, enabling extraction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100% fee on input: entire input becomes fee, amountOut=0. No extraction possible — user just loses their input. This is documented behavior in FeeHelper (line 63-64 of SwapMath). Not exploitable since caller voluntarily sends tokens to a 100% fee pool.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5: uint256 to uint128 truncation in _getTokensOwed allows over-claiming fees
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Theoretical: with max feeGrowth delta (2^256-1) and max liquidity (2^128-1), mulDiv result exceeds uint128. Practical: feeGrowthGlobal bounded by total fees/liquidity ratio — requires unrealistic fee accumulation (~2^128 tokens in fees). Not practically exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H6: Division before multiplication truncates intermediate result, reducing fees or inflating output
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All critical paths use FullMath.mulDiv which performs multiplication before division (512-bit intermediate). Verified: mulDiv(3, 7, 5) = 4 (correct), vs division-first: 3/5*7 = 0 (truncated). No division-before-multiplication patterns found in fee or swap math.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H7: swapExtraData != 32 bytes causes silent default via assembly calldataload
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: If swapExtraData.length != 32, the code silently uses default values (documented behavior). This is not exploitable — default values are safe, and the caller who provides wrong-length data only hurts themselves.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H11: Low-liquidity prime/exploit/reset loop — harvest 1-wei truncation per iteration across 100+ swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100 iterations at liquidity=1 with 1-wei input and 0.3% fee: total extracted output = 0. At minimum liquidity, rounding always rounds output to 0. No dust accumulation possible.

theft_theses.thesis: Craft tick_index overflow to produce near-zero sqrt price, then add minimal liquidity and withdraw massive amounts (Cetus pattern)
Find wrong-direction rounding in any division, perform 1000+ sequential 1-wei operations to accumulate dust (Balancer pattern)
First depositor deposits 1 wei, donates to inflate share price, second depositor gets 0 shares (ERC-4626 pattern)
Deploy malicious hook returning price=0 to SingleProviderPoolType, bypass swap calculations (Balancer rate provider pattern)
100% fee on input but not output creates asymmetric extraction path
uint256->uint128 truncation in _getTokensOwed allows over-claiming accumulated fees
Swap round-trip A->B->A produces profit due to rounding
CLOB calculateFixedInput rounds UP output, allowing taker to extract value from maker
Exact tick boundary crossing causes liquidity to not be properly added/removed, creating ghost liquidity
Division before multiplication in fee path truncates intermediate, user pays less fee
Low-liquidity dust loop: add 1 wei liq -> swap -> collect truncation dust -> repeat 100+ times for compounded profit
